featured_reviews.name: Batul Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Poor service, missing Nalli, and arrogant management.

I wanted to rate higher based on taste, but a2-star rating is all I can give due to the poor service and unprofessional attitude of the owner. I ordered the Nalli Nihari, and the actual 'Nalli' (bone marrow) was missing, replaced by a bowl of oil and mashed-up bone fragments.
When shown evidence, the attendant refused to accept the shortcoming, instead the owner started bragging about being in the business for 5 years and arguing that this is 'how it's served.' Offering a discount for the missing component is not a substitute for serving the dish correctly. It was condescending to be told how to eat a dish I know well.

Furthermore, I witnessed the staff acting defensive until a large group of men at another table pointed out similar faults, at which point they immediately complied. Customer service should be equal for everyone, not based on intimidation.

It is arrogant to assume customers do not know quality, especially when trying to pass off sub-par plating as authentic. The owner needs to learn that constructive feedback is not an attack. I hope they improve in the next 5 years, but I will not be returning.

Even after admitting the fault by discounting the dish, the owner argued rather than apologizing. It’s clear they don’t take feedback well and prioritize being right over serving quality food. Poor experience, would not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Gulshan Siddiqui
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered the Nihari, their famous Chicken Peshawari, and the Chicken Malai Leg. To be honest, I feel this place is just overhyped by influencers. The food was very average… I would even say below average.

After waiting for almost an hour, the taste really did not justify the hype at all. It felt like the popularity comes more from paid promotions than the actual quality of food.

I personally would not recommend coming here. There are many better places to eat. I waited so long only to end up eating tasteless food, and I definitely won’t be coming back again.

featured_reviews.name: Savita Nangare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I seriously doubt the authenticity of the positive reviews posted here. We hired this catering agency for a small, close-knit gathering and, based on the reviews, expected high-quality food. Unfortunately, the experience was terrible.
The food taste was extremely poor, and the quantity and quality of sweets provided were extremely limited and disappointing. Several people from our group complained of diarrhoea afterward, and I personally suffered from it for days.
When I shared this feedback with the owner, he was dismissive and clearly uninterested in taking responsibility or even acknowledging the issue.
A word of caution: do not rely blindly on online reviews when choosing caterers. They can be misleading, and our experience proves that firsthand.

featured_reviews.name: Shams sayed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at Babji Caterers on the 25th Ramzan night.
We first ordered Butter Garlic Seekh, but the taste was completely off. The menu combination felt forced and the flavors were not in sync at all.
Then we ordered a Chicken Roll and Chicken Zafrani Tikka (yellow sauce dipped). The tikka had a very distinct beef-like texture, smell, and taste. When we asked the waiter, he insisted it was chicken, but honestly it did not taste like chicken at all. The chicken roll was just okish, nothing special.
Lastly, we ordered plain seekh, thinking at least that would be good. But surprisingly, even that didn’t taste good. Seekh is something that usually tastes amazing everywhere, but this is the first time I didn’t like seekh anywhere.
The place is overpriced, seating is just average, and the food quality doesn’t justify the price. Instead of spending here, you can easily go to a proper restaurant, sit comfortably, and have much tastier food for the same price.
₹350 for a seekh in Bhatiyar Khana feels like full-on loot.
Not recommended. Save your money.

featured_reviews.name: M K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Babji, Byculla, Mumbai, Sitafalwadi Road Babji in Byculla is a must-see if you're an avid foodie! Especially during their Ramazan setup for iftaari, we enjoyed an amazing meal. Despite having a small menu, every meal is really amazing.
The evening's highlight was without a doubt the **Fish Masala Fry**, which we began with. The fish was melt-in-your-mouth, well-seasoned, and cooked to perfection.
In addition, the **Gurda Masala, Bheja Masala, Nalli Bihari, and Chicken Barra** were expertly prepared and bursting with flavor. With its rich, fragrant spices and succulent, juicy meat, each dish was a perfect example of real Mughlai and North Indian cooking.
In addition to the main courses, we sampled the **Keema, Seekh, Bheja, and Naan Sandwich**, which was incredibly flavorful in every mouthful. The meat of the **Nihari** was exceptionally delicate and perfectly slow-cooked, making it stand out.
We had **Jalebi, Kunafa, and Malpuwa** for sweets, and they were all delicious. Our lunch was perfectly concluded with the **Kunafa**, which was specifically created by the kind and hospitable host.
The texture and sweetness were perfectly balanced!
Excellent service, food quality, and seating arrangements were all provided. To ensure we had the greatest experience, the staff was amiable and considerate.
We felt completely at home thanks to the gracious welcome. All things considered, Babji is a secret treasure for lovers of hearty, tasty cuisine.
This establishment will satisfy your cravings for meats, grills, or rich desserts. Highly recommended, especially the **Kunafa** and **Fish Masala Fry**! I'm looking forward to returning soon.
